public_rationale: Marcus says recent systems can be left to run more on their own. On 19 December 2025, METR estimated that Claude Opus 4.5 had a 50% time horizon of about 4 hours 49 minutes on its tasks. METR called this its highest published time horizon to date (e1). On 5 February 2026, Anthropic said Opus 4.6 'sustains agentic tasks for longer' than its predecessor (e2). This is a company claim, not a measurement. The record METR figure was at the 50% success level. At the 80% level, Opus 4.5's time horizon was 27 minutes, which METR said was similar to past models and below GPT-5.1-Codex-Max's 32 minutes (e1). A LessWrong commentary described the 80% horizon as essentially flat since GPT-5.1-Codex-Max (e3). So the evidence shows longer tasks completed at the 50% level, but not a matching gain in reliable completion.
limitations: 'Let things rip more' is informal and has no threshold, so it is judged against task-length measures.
The METR figures come from a LessWrong reproduction of METR's thread. The 95% confidence interval for the 50% horizon is wide, from 1 hr 49 mins to 20 hrs 25 mins.
Anthropic's statement about Opus 4.6 is a company disclosure. METR measurements of Opus 4.6 were published after the post and are not used here.

our_interpretation: 'Recently' is read as the few months before the post, roughly late 2025 to early February 2026.
'Let things rip more' is read as: recent coding agents can work on longer tasks with less human help than earlier systems.
criteria.support_condition: Measurements or credible disclosures from late 2025 to early 2026 show recent models handling longer autonomous coding tasks than their predecessors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Measurements from the period show no meaningful gain in autonomous task length or success for the newest models over earlier ones.
